title: Workout for People with Higher Body Weight (Knee-Friendly)
intro: You don't need to lose weight first to start exercising, and you don't need to jump around either. This no-impact routine uses only a chair and a wall, so it's kinder on your knees.
muscles: Thighs, glutes, core, chest and shoulders. It also trains your heart without impact on your knees and ankles.
steps: Warm-up: march on the spot for 2 minutes, you can hold a chair or do it seated.
Sit-to-stand: sit on a chair, stand up using your legs, sit back down slowly. 8-10 times.
Wall push-up: hands on the wall at shoulder height, bend your elbows, push back. 8-10 times.
Step tap: tap your foot to the front and to the side, alternating. 20 times each side.
Repeat for 2 rounds, then go for a relaxed 10-minute walk if you can.
mistakes: Starting straight away with jogging or jumping. Repeated impact can make your knees hurt.
Knees caving inwards when getting up from the chair. Make sure your knees stay in line with your toes.
Doing too much on day one until your whole body aches, then giving up. A little but often is better.
easier: Do all moves seated: seated march, arm raises, alternate leg straightening. Use a higher chair and hold a table to stand up.
harder: Use a lower chair, lower slowly in 3 seconds, add a third round, and extend your walk to 20-30 minutes.
dose: 10-20 minutes, 3-5 days a week. Start with 2 rounds and add a little each week when you feel comfortable.
safety: If you have diabetes, high blood pressure, heart problems or long-term knee pain, see a doctor before starting. Stop if you have chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, or knee swelling and sharp pain.

faq.q: Do I need to lose weight first before I can exercise?
faq.a: No need. The right exercise for your current level is safe and good for your health. Start with easy moves and build up slowly.

faq.q: My knees make a sound when I get up from the chair. Is it dangerous?
faq.a: Sounds without pain are usually nothing to worry about. But if the sound comes with pain, swelling or your knee feels unstable, stop and see a doctor or physio.

Walking is a great start. Add simple strength exercises like the ones above so your leg muscles get stronger and support your knees. Fat comes off from a combination of eating and overall movement, not from one body part only.
